title: introduce response_format.strict_level and structured error mapping for schema failures
author: Lina Park
body:
Motivation: Customers need predictable failure modes when asking the runtime to emit structured JSON. Existing JSON schema validation is brittle for streaming outputs and offers little control over whether validation problems fail the request or are surfaced as warnings. This PR introduces a lightweight per-request and per-route strictness control (response_format.strict_level) and a standard error-mapping produced when schema validation fails in streaming or non-streaming modes.

Summary of changes: adds response_format.strict_level with values (off|warn|error); implements streaming-aware partial validation that can buffer and attempt recovery for warn mode; defines a canonical structured error report (error_code, location, token_snippet, suggestion, transient) that the OpenAI-compat layer emits on schema issues; maps schema failures to HTTP 400/422 when strict_level=error.

Design notes: the strict_level flag is evaluated in this order: explicit request param > route config > org default. warn mode attempts streaming-friendly heuristics (buffer up to N tokens, attempt incremental re-parse, if still invalid emit structured error record to the metadata channel and continue if possible). error mode will abort the stream and surface the structured error as the final message in the error channel. off preserves current behavior (best-effort, may emit textual hints in the stream). The structured error format is intentionally compact and platform-neutral to support SDKs and downstream tracing.

Compatibility: default remains off; no user-visible changes for callers who don't set strict_level. OpenAI-compat layer supports the new fields under the "response_format" envelope (backwards compatible). SDKs updated to expose the enum and helper utilities to decode the structured error payload.

Testing & rollout: unit tests for validator edge cases and integration tests for streaming scenarios are included. Feature will be rolled out behind a runtime flag and enabled for a small percentage of traffic for two weeks before full release. Documentation was added and linked in the files_changed list.

Files changed (high level): new validator and policy integration + compatibility glue in the API gateway; SDK updates in Python and TypeScript; docs and changelog.

Related: ENG-1124 (structured-output roadmap), ENG-1187 (streaming stability work). See inline commits for details.
commits: feat(api): accept response_format.strict_level in request parsing and validation
feat(stream): implement partial/streaming-aware jsonschema validator with buffer window
chore(openai-compat): emit structured schema errors on validation failures
feat(sdk): expose StrictLevel enum and structured error helper in python + ts sdks
test: add integration tests for warn/error/off modes and streaming fallback
docs: document response_format.strict_level and migration guidance
review_comments: Marco: Can you clarify how route-level defaults are configured? Response: added policy integration and config examples in strictness_policy.go and docs.

Priya: Concern about increased latency in warn mode due to buffering. Response: buffer window limited to 256 tokens and bounded by time (50ms); added perf tests and benchmark results to bench/stream_validator_bench.go.
Evan: SDK ergonomics - prefer enum helpers. Response: added StrictLevel helpers and a convenience decoder in both python and ts sdks.
release_notes: Introduces response_format.strict_level (off, warn, error) to control JSON schema enforcement behavior. Adds a canonical structured error payload for schema validation failures that SDKs can decode. Streaming validator will attempt recoveries in warn mode and will abort with clear structured errors in error mode. Default behavior unchanged (off).
